title: Why Is the Sky Blue?
end_card: Because air scatters blue light far more than red.

scenes.speaker: leo
scenes.voice: Why is the sky blue? It's just air.
scenes.subtitle: Why is the sky blue? It's just air.

scenes.speaker: mia
scenes.voice: Sunlight looks white, but it's really every color mixed together.
scenes.subtitle: Sunlight looks white, but it's really every color mixed together.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.voice: When that light hits the air, blue scatters about five times more than red.
scenes.subtitle: When that light hits the air, blue scatters about 5x more than red.

overlays.text: more scattering for blue than for red

scenes.speaker: leo
scenes.voice: So the sky is just scattered sunlight?
scenes.subtitle: So the sky is just scattered sunlight?!

scenes.speaker: mia
scenes.voice: Exactly. Blue reaches your eyes from every direction.
scenes.subtitle: Exactly. Blue reaches your eyes from every direction.

scenes.speaker: narrator
scenes.voice: At sunset, light crosses much more air. Most of the blue scatters away, and the reds are left.
scenes.subtitle: At sunset, light crosses much more air. Most of the blue scatters away, and the reds are left.

scenes.speaker: mia
scenes.voice: Next time you look up, you're looking at physics.
scenes.subtitle: Next time you look up, you're looking at physics.
